free_tier.stated: USD 100 one-time credit when a payment method is added; Starter plan is USD 0 plus usage beyond the credit
free_tier.notes: The credit is released only after a card or Link wallet passes a USD 0 authorization; no card means no credit. Credits are spent at the standard per-unit rates.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a virtual machine, not an object store; the first 5 GiB of sandbox disk is included

retention.stated: A paused sandbox keeps its files and memory; a non-sticky session is paused automatically at its maximum duration; disks are wiped on teardown; persistent volumes and snapshots are managed separately.

egress.terms: not published: the pricing rate card lists vCPU, memory, disk and storage with no outbound transfer allowance or per-GB price; the sandbox page states 'Tunneled, authenticated connections. No public IPs.'

interface_detail: The `luxor` CLI and Go, TypeScript and Python SDKs against https://api.luxor.ai; the sandbox CLI reference documents port exposure and SSH into a session. No public IP is assigned.
tooling: curl -fsSL https://luxor.ai/install.sh | sh installs the CLI; SDKs are npm install @luxorai/sandbox, pip install luxor-ai and go get go.luxor.ai/sandbox.
chaining: Creates isolated full Linux VMs for agent tasks with snapshots and persistent volumes; hosted only, with no user-owned hardware involved.

limits.value: Starter caps a machine at 4 cores / 8 GB RAM, 5 concurrent sessions and 100 GiB of workspace storage; raises to 16 cores / 64 GB, 100 sessions and 1,000 GiB on Team
at the concurrency limit a job queues rather than fails; a Starter job targeting a larger size is blocked rather than queued
when the workspace has no usable credit, new jobs and sessions are rejected until a top-up of at least $20 or auto-reload

limits_note: Sandbox rates beyond the credit are $0.00084 per vCPU-minute, $0.00027 per GiB-minute, $0.0000018 per GiB-minute of disk after the first 5 GiB, and $0.20 per GiB-month of storage from the first byte. Billing is per second with no minimums.
binding_note: The USD 100 credit and the Starter machine ceiling bind first: credit covers roughly 25,000 minutes on a 2 vCPU runner and a larger Starter size is blocked until a payment method is on file.

identity_cost.detail: Registration starts GitHub sign-up at app.luxor.ai/auth/registration; the USD 100 credit requires adding a card or Link wallet from the Billing tab, and Stripe verifies it with a USD 0 authorization. The registration page itself shows no separate email, phone or ID gate.

reliability_note: SSD disks are mounted from Ceph; a sandbox is not paused for inactivity, so a running session accrues charges until paused or terminated; jobs are balance-gated and stop starting when credit runs out. Auto-reload adds $20 when the balance drops below $5.
confidence_note: The credit gate, per-second rates, plan ceilings, card check, concurrency and no-public-IP statement are quoted from first-party pages read on 2026-11-24.

evidence.proved: everything is billed per second with no minimums and no queue charge
evidence.quote: Everything is billed per second, with no minimums or per-seat fees. Compute is quoted per minute, storage per month and code reviews per review.

evidence.proved: the credit needs a card or Link wallet verified by a USD 0 authorization, and auto-reload adds USD 20 below USD 5
evidence.quote: Create your account, then add a card or Link wallet from the workspace's [Billing tab](/docs/account/payment). Stripe verifies the card with a $0 authorization, and the workspace receives a one-time **$100 credit**.

evidence.proved: auto-reload adds USD 20 when the balance drops below USD 5
evidence.quote: Adding the payment method also turns on auto-reload, which adds $20 whenever your balance drops below $5.

evidence.proved: USD 100 buys about 25,000 minutes on a 2 vCPU runner at USD 0.002 per vCPU-minute
evidence.quote: For a 2 vCPU x64 runner billed at **$0.002 per vCPU / minute**, $100 in credits buys roughly **25,000 minutes**.

evidence.proved: when the balance runs out, new jobs and sessions stop until a top-up of at least USD 20 or auto-reload
evidence.quote: When your balance runs out, Luxor Agent Cloud stops starting new jobs and sessions until you top up (minimum $20) or turn on auto-reload.

evidence.proved: sandboxes have no public IPs and are wiped on teardown
evidence.quote:
### Wiped on teardown

Disk and memory are gone when the session ends.

### Secrets never cross boundaries

Credentials are scoped to one session.

### Encrypted in transit

Tunneled, authenticated connections. No public IPs.

evidence.proved: a running sandbox is not paused for inactivity and accrues compute charges until paused or terminated
evidence.quote: Sandboxes are not paused for inactivity: a running sandbox accrues compute charges until you pause or terminate it, or until a non-sticky session reaches its maximum duration and is paused.

evidence.proved: the shared concurrency limit is 5 on Starter and 100 on Team, and jobs above it queue rather than fail
evidence.quote:
| Starter    | Up to 5                       |
| Team       | Up to 100                     |
| Enterprise | Custom (unlimited on request) |
For a new user, the Luxor Agent Cloud-owned URL starts GitHub sign-up directly; the user can choose another sign-in method if needed.

notes: A hosted sandbox lane of the same platform that sells GitHub Actions runners and AI code review. The USD 100 credit is released only after a USD 0 card authorization, so an email alone cannot spend it; egress has no published rate. Self-hosting is not offered for this service.

shape.note: Starter ceiling of 4 cores / 8 GB RAM and 100 GiB workspace storage; 2 vCPU is one physical core

extras.billing_model: per-second usage against a one-time credit on the free Starter plan
extras.term: Starter has no monthly fee; Team is $250 monthly or $200 yearly
extras.price_arithmetic: $0.00084 per vCPU-minute plus $0.00027 per GiB-minute, with the first 5 GiB of disk included

network_out.ports: no public IPs; port exposure is documented in the CLI

session_cap.note: a non-sticky session is paused at an unstated maximum duration; no inactivity pause for sandboxes
